item.title: Uizard
item.description:
Uizard generates editable UI mockups from text prompts, hand-drawn sketches, or screenshots, letting non-designers produce a workable prototype and hand developers something closer to spec than a napkin drawing.

Why it stands out

  • Sketch-to-UI conversion, turning a photographed whiteboard wireframe into an editable digital layout.
  • Text-prompt design generation for teams that want to start from a description rather than a blank canvas.
  • Theme and rebranding tools that restyle an entire mockup’s color and typography in one pass.

Good for

Founders, PMs, and non-designers who need a credible UI prototype fast, without starting a Figma file from scratch.

item.title: Google Stitch
item.description: Google acquired Galileo AI in 2025 and folded its UI-generation engine into Google Labs as Stitch — a Gemini-powered tool that turns a short text description or an uploaded wireframe into polished, editable interface designs, complete with exportable front-end code.

item.title: Figma Make
item.description: Figma Make builds on Figma’s design surface directly, letting teams turn a prompt or an existing frame into an interactive prototype, and iterate on it with follow-up prompts without leaving Figma.

item.title: Magic Patterns
item.description: Magic Patterns turns a text prompt or rough sketch into a working React UI, aimed at product managers and designers who want to validate an idea’s interface before it becomes an engineering ticket.

item.title: Polymet
item.description: Polymet generates multi-screen product design concepts from a text prompt, giving product designers a set of coherent, on-brand screens to react to and refine instead of starting ideation from a blank file.

item.title: Visily
item.description: Visily specializes in getting a rough idea into an editable wireframe fast — importing screenshots of existing apps, sketches, or prompts and turning them into a design that non-designers can still rearrange and present.
